sections.h2: Where is McIntosh County and what is it known for?
sections.html:
McIntosh County is in east central Oklahoma and its county seat is Eufaula. It covers 712 square miles, and 13 percent of that is water, mostly Eufaula Lake, the largest reservoir entirely within Oklahoma. The 2020 Census counted 18,941 residents.

The Deep Fork, North Canadian and Canadian rivers drain the county. Neighbors are Muskogee, Haskell, Pittsburg, Hughes, Okfuskee and Okmulgee counties. The county sits mostly inside the Muscogee (Creek) Nation, with the far east inside the Cherokee Nation.

sections.h2: What is the history of McIntosh County?
sections.html:
The county is named for the Creek McIntosh family, who led the Lower Towns to Indian Territory after the 1825 Treaty of Indian Springs. North Fork Town was founded in 1836 on the Texas Road, about two miles east of present-day Eufaula.

The Missouri-Kansas-Texas Railway came through in 1871 and 1872, which established Checotah and Eufaula. The Battle of Honey Springs, the largest Civil War battle in what is now Oklahoma, was fought near Rentiesville. The county was created at statehood in 1907, and a dispute known as the McIntosh County Seat War between Checotah and Eufaula ended with Eufaula named the permanent seat.

sections.h2: What does the McIntosh County economy and housing stock look like?
sections.html:
The economy rested on farming and ranching, and cattle remain important. Building Eufaula Lake, completed in 1964, flooded much of the best cropland, then brought hydroelectric power, tourism, boat building and retail. Oil, gas, limestone, sand and gravel have also mattered.

The housing numbers stand out. The 2020 Census found 11,755 housing units in the county and 32.4 percent of them vacant, a share well above nearby counties such as Muskogee at 12.8 percent. The median age was 49.5 and 26.9 percent of residents were 65 or older.

sections.h2: Which roads and towns serve McIntosh County?
sections.html:
Interstate 40 and US 69 cross the county, with US 266, State Highways 9 and 72 and the Indian Nation Turnpike also serving it. Checotah and Eufaula are the cities. Hanna, Hitchita, Rentiesville, Stidham and Vernon are towns, and Duchess Landing, Shady Grove and Texanna are census-designated places.

Checotah is the nearest city to Lake Eufaula State Park. Interstate 40 is the main east-west route through the county.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in McIntosh County?
sections.html:
The Assessor is Jennifer Ballard, in office since 2025. The Treasurer is Kimberly Smelser. Their jobs follow the state pattern: the assessor values property, files the roll, and the treasurer collects.

Board meetings moved to the courthouse at 110 N. 1st Street in Eufaula starting November 9, 2026. The treasurer's page links the assessor's ACTDataScout site for parcel locations and values. See the treasurer page and the assessor page.

sections.h2: What do McIntosh County sellers usually face?
sections.html:
The typical seller here owns an older rural house, a lake-area property, an inherited home or a property that has been empty for a while. About 27 percent of residents are 65 or older, so estate sales and downsizing are common reasons to sell.

Timing around tax dates matters. If you are selling between November and March, find out whether the first half has been paid, since the treasurer cannot accept a first-half payment after December 31.

sections.h2: Which McIntosh County details do sellers often overlook?
sections.html:
Several small points trip people up. Mortgage companies usually remit through a third-party tax service, so confirm the service actually paid before assuming the bill is cleared. A delinquent personal lien blocks a mortgage payment until it is satisfied. And the treasurer states that delinquent taxes must all be paid together, so one unpaid year cannot be skipped.

The county also sits inside two tribal jurisdictions, the Muscogee (Creek) Nation across most of it and the Cherokee Nation in the far east. That does not change how the county bills property tax, but it is a reason to ask the title company about the specifics of any parcel before listing or signing.

  • Ask the treasurer for a written payoff, including all delinquent years.
  • Ask the assessor to confirm the parcel's mailing address and classification.
  • Ask the title company to check for liens before you accept a price.

sections.h2: How is a McIntosh County tax bill built from the assessment?
sections.html:
The assessor values property and certifies the roll after the Excise Board sets millage. The treasurer then collects one combined bill for the county, cities and towns, and schools. One mill is $1 per $1,000 of taxable value, and Oklahoma Policy Institute says assessment ratios are 10 to 15 percent.

Statewide, the homestead exemption takes $1,000 off taxable value of a primary home, and a home's assessed value cannot rise more than 3 percent a year unless it sells. Lake-area second homes do not get the homestead deduction because it applies only to a primary residence.

  • Value: assessor.
  • Levies: each taxing body, certified by the Excise Board.
  • Collection: treasurer.

sections.h2: What are McIntosh County's due dates, interest and new-owner steps?
sections.html:
Pay at least half by December 31, and the second half by March 31. Miss the first half and the whole bill goes delinquent on January 1. Balances over $25 can be paid in two installments, and the treasurer does not mail second-half notices.

  • Interest is 18 percent per year, added monthly on the 16th day at 1.5 percent.
  • Not receiving a statement is not a legal reason to waive interest.
  • A new owner should give the assessor a mailing address before September 30, before accounts are certified to the treasurer.
  • Mortgage companies often pay through a tax service, so a paid bill can take time to appear.
  • All delinquent taxes must be paid at the same time.

A personal lien on a property can also block a mortgage company's payment until the lien is satisfied.

sections.h2: How do you protest a McIntosh County valuation?
sections.html:
You have 30 calendar days from the mailing date of an increase notice to file a written protest with the assessor. For an unchanged valuation, file by the first Monday in April.

The assessor holds an informal hearing and sends a written decision within 7 calendar days. You then have 15 days to appeal to the county board of equalization. The assessor also runs a four-year visual inspection program, so a recent drive-by inspection can explain a changed value.

Under the state rules, a primary home's assessed value cannot rise more than 3 percent per year unless it sells, and the homestead exemption is $1,000 off taxable value.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a McIntosh County house with tax due?
sections.html:
Taxes owed are settled at closing from sale proceeds, so ask the treasurer for a current payoff. Lakefront and lake-area homes, aging rural houses and inherited properties all show up in this county, and many need repairs that a retail buyer's lender would not accept.

A cash purchase as-is avoids lender-driven repair demands. If back taxes, a probate or a vacant house is the issue, getting a straight payoff figure first lets you compare options sensibly.

faqs.q: Who is the McIntosh County assessor?
faqs.a: Jennifer Ballard is the McIntosh County Assessor, reachable at 918-689-2611.

faqs.q: When are McIntosh County property taxes due?
faqs.a: At least half is due by December 31 and the second half by March 31. Missing the December 31 first-half date makes the whole amount delinquent.

faqs.q: What interest does McIntosh County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: The treasurer adds 1.5 percent per month, which the office describes as 18 percent per year, on the 16th of each month.

faqs.q: Where do I file a homestead exemption in McIntosh County?
faqs.a: Homestead and other exemptions are filed with the County Assessor, not the treasurer.

faqs.q: Do I need to tell McIntosh County about a new address after buying?
faqs.a: Yes. New owners should give the assessor the correct mailing address before September 30 so the statement reaches them.
